summary: Tested the new AI-coach write-action (POST /api/coach/chat with <ADD_EXERCISE> tag) and the new current_session context field. Wrote two suites: (1) 18 pure-function unit tests for validate_coach_added_exercise + _sanitize_text — ALL 18 PASS, proving name-required, category-coercion-to-accessory, sets clamp 1..10, reps default '8-10', notes cap 200, HTML strip, and case-insensitive category all work correctly. (2) 7 end-to-end LLM tests hitting the real endpoint — ALL 7 FAIL with HTTP 500 because the upstream Emergent proxy rejects EMERGENT_LLM_KEY as 'Invalid API key'. This is a CREDENTIAL/CONFIG issue (the placeholder key '[REDACTED_KEY]' in /app/backend/.env and .env.local is not valid). Behavioural E2E of the new add-exercise flow, category handling, malformed-input safety, no-false-trigger, current_session freshness, and PROGRAM_CHANGE regression could NOT be verified against the live LLM until the key is fixed. Secondary robustness gap: coach_chat has no try/except around chat.send_message, so upstream LLM auth/timeouts surface as naked 500s to the client instead of a graceful 502/503.

critical.issue: EMERGENT_LLM_KEY in /app/backend/.env and /app/backend/.env.local is '[REDACTED_KEY]' which the upstream proxy rejects: litellm.AuthenticationError 'Invalid API key'. Every coach call returns HTTP 500 — impossible to E2E-verify the new add-exercise write-action, category handling, current_session honouring, or PROGRAM_CHANGE regression against the real LLM. Backend log evidence: /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log — 'openai.AuthenticationError: Invalid API key' → 'emergentintegrations.llm.chat.ChatError'.

No try/except around `await chat.send_message(...)` at server.py:4223. Any upstream LLM error (auth, rate-limit, timeout, network) leaks as HTTP 500 instead of a graceful error payload. Should catch ChatError and return 502/503 with {response: 'Coach is temporarily unavailable', added_exercise: null, ...} so the client can degrade instead of showing red-screen.

minor.issue: _sanitize_text() is applied to `current_session` at server.py:3963 via re.sub(r"[\x00-\x1f\x7f]", ' ') + re.sub(r'\s+', ' ') — this collapses ALL newlines/tabs in the client snapshot into single spaces, so the coach receives a run-on line ('Exercises the athlete added to today: - Face Pulls [accessory] (3 sets) Sets logged so far today: - Back Squat: 315 x5') instead of the structured multi-line block the client sent. Still parseable by the LLM but structure is lost; consider a snapshot-specific sanitiser that preserves \n while stripping other control chars, or increase the 3000-char cap awareness.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix EMERGENT_LLM_KEY. Current value '[REDACTED_KEY]' in both /app/backend/.env and /app/backend/.env.local is rejected by the upstream proxy as 'Invalid API key'. Once a valid key is in place, re-run pytest backend/tests/test_coach_add_exercise.py to verify all 6 behavioural scenarios (happy-path add, category, malformed, no-false-trigger, current_session freshness, PROGRAM_CHANGE regression).

HIGH: Wrap `await chat.send_message(...)` in coach_chat (server.py ~4223) in try/except ChatError → return 200/503 with a safe fallback payload (added_exercise=null, response='Coach is temporarily unavailable, try again') instead of leaking 500 to the client. Same treatment likely wanted at the other 8+ send_message call sites (5585, 5645, 6094, 6586, 7067, 7177, 3032).

MINOR: Consider a newline-preserving sanitiser for `current_session` so the multi-line client snapshot (added-exercises + logged sets) reaches the LLM with its bullet structure intact — the current _sanitize_text collapses it to one line.
Once the LLM key is fixed, main agent should self-run: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_coach_add_exercise.py -v — the 7 tests already retry LLM non-determinism up to 3× per scenario.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:3672 validate_coach_added_exercise is well-designed — fails closed on missing name, clamps sets to 1..10, coerces unknown category to 'accessory', caps notes at 200 chars. All 18 unit tests pass.

server.py:4242 <ADD_EXERCISE> parser correctly (a) strips the tag from user-visible text regardless of JSON validity, (b) returns added_exercise=null on malformed JSON, (c) appends a plain-text fallback nudge when payload is unusable so the coach doesn't falsely claim success. Good.
server.py:4255 id prefix 'added-ex-' + uuid.hex[:12] matches spec and mirrors the client-side manual-add shape.

server.py:3961-3969 current_session context is guarded (only injected when non-empty after sanitisation) and clearly framed to the LLM as superseding the prescribed session. Good design — but see minor issue about newline collapse.
server.py:4223 no exception handling around LlmChat.send_message is a robustness gap unrelated to this feature but exposed by the current invalid LLM key.

The system prompt block at server.py:4180 clearly documents the write-action contract (single block, valid category set, sets 1-10, reps free-form) and instructs the model to confirm what was added in prose — matches backend parser expectations.

rca_of_issue: RCA of the 7 E2E failures — NOT a bug in the new add-exercise feature: (1) reproduction: POST /api/coach/chat with any valid message + Bearer token → HTTP 500. (2) backend.err.log shows litellm→openai auth path returning 'Invalid API key'. (3) EMERGENT_LLM_KEY in /app/backend/.env (line 25) and /app/backend/.env.local both equal '[REDACTED_KEY]' — a short placeholder-looking value that the emergent proxy does not recognise. (4) mitigation: provision a real EMERGENT_LLM_KEY in /app/backend/.env.local (which is gitignored, per .env comment) then `sudo supervisorctl restart backend`. Additionally, adding try/except around chat.send_message would prevent this class of failure from surfacing as HTTP 500 to clients.
